title: Topic catalyst register - what each tracked topic actually settles on
read_this_way: These are not news items. Each row is the settlement reference the exchange itself names for a series, read straight out of GET /series/{series_ticker}. A price jump is only 'explained' when the referenced feed published something at that moment; this file tells you where to look, it does not claim a cause.

primary_source.field: settlement_sources[].{name,url}, contract_terms_url, fee_type, fee_multiplier, category, tags
primary_source.note: Every entry below was read from a live 200 response on 2026-11-20 (UTC) by this session; the console also fetches these per-series records for any series it tracks, so a stale file here only degrades the fallback list, never the per-alert links.

sources.label: ICE - WTI front-month settlement prices (named settlement source for KXWTIMAX)
sources.rule_quote: If ICE reports that the maximum price of oil (as defined exclusively by the set of WTI front-month settle prices) is above $180 between Issuance and Dec 31, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
sources.why_it_matters: A printed ICE settle outside the expected band is the only thing that moves a max/min-of-settles contract; a swing without an ICE publication is demo liquidity, not news.

sources.label: EIA weekly gasoline prices (reference for the retail-gas series KXWTIREF, not re-fetched in this run)
sources.kind: underlying reference for a sibling series
sources.verified_by: an earlier verification of GET /series/KXWTIREF in this session; the series record was not re-fetched on 2026-11-20 (the fetch errored), so treat the link as unconfirmed
sources.irregularity: The EIA weekly U.S. Regular series publishes Wednesdays ~1 pm ET for the prior week; KXWTIREF asks for a daily national average, and the 2026 holiday schedule also moves one release to Monday. A daily-reference feed is therefore expected to be the EIA *daily* series or a retail survey, not this weekly page. Flagged rather than smoothed over.

sources.label: Republican Party (named settlement source for KXPRESNOM* family)
Democratic Party (named settlement source for KXPRESNOMD)
sources.rule_quote: If Hunter Biden wins and accepts the nomination for the Presidency for the Democratic party, then the market resolves to Yes.
sources.why_it_matters: Nomination markets settle on a party's own certification or an acceptance statement, so a party press release - not a poll - is the event that should move price.

sources.label: Contract terms PDF (what counts as 'wins and accepts')
sources.verified_by: session 5ab18dc3, contract_terms_url on the KXPRESNOMD series record

sources.label: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences (named settlement source for KXOSCARPIC)
sources.rule_quote: If Digger has won Best Picture at the 99th Academy Awards, then the market resolves to Yes.
sources.product_note: The series record carries an important-information block: only one Yes outcome is allowed and a tie resolves the separate 'Tie' market to Yes. Any alert near a tie announcement should be read against that clause.
sources.why_it_matters: Oscar markets move on nominations/winner announcements from the Academy (and, for the betting-relevant 'will be nominated' style markets, the Oscar shortlists), not on review sentiment.

sources.label: Contract terms PDF (Oscars)
sources.verified_by: session 5ab18dc3, contract_terms_url on the KXOSCARPIC series record

sources.label: CF Benchmarks (named settlement source for KXBTCY)
sources.rule_quote: If the simple average of the sixty seconds of CF Benchmarks' BRTI before 12 AM EST is between 120000.00-124999.99 at 12 AM EST on Jan 1, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.
sources.why_it_matters: Settlement is the 60-second BRTI average before the timestamp, so the last minute of the reference index - not the spot print you are looking at - decides these markets. Rounding at a bucket edge (e.g. 124999.5) is where demo price and settlement can legitimately disagree.

sources.label: Contract terms PDF (Crypto)
sources.verified_by: session 5ab18dc3, contract_terms_url on the KXBTCY series record

sources.label: the Governing League - PGA TOUR (named settlement source for KXPGATOUR)
sources.rule_quote: If Taylor Moore wins the The RSM Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
sources.why_it_matters: A win market settles on the final leaderboard; weather delays, a playoff, or a scorecard correction are the announcements that move it. Round-to-round leader changes move price but not the outcome.
